question: A 4430-g (9-lb 10-oz) male newborn is delivered at term to a 27-year-old woman, gravida 2, para 1. The second stage of labor was prolonged and required vacuum-assisted vaginal delivery. Apgar scores are 9 and 10 at 1 and 5 minutes, respectively. Examination of the neonate 2 hours later shows a soft, nonpulsatile swelling over the left parietal bone that does not cross suture lines. Vital signs are within normal limits. The pupils are equal and reactive to light. The lungs are clear to auscultation. Heart sounds are normal. The spine is normal. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

paths: (Pressure- physical agent)-CAUSES->(Pneumonia)-CAUSES->(Chronic empyema)-CAUSES->(Radionuclide Imaging)-DIAGNOSES->(Cephalhematoma due to birth trauma)
(Pressure- physical agent)-CAUSES->(Coronary Arteriosclerosis)-CAUSES->(Coronary angiography)-ISA->(Radionuclide Imaging)-DIAGNOSES->(Cephalhematoma due to birth trauma)
(Left parietal bone)-LOCATION_OF->(Radionuclide Imaging)-DIAGNOSES->(Cephalhematoma due to birth trauma)
(Left parietal bone)-LOCATION_OF->(Radionuclide Imaging)-DIAGNOSES->(Cephalhematoma due to birth trauma)

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Prolonged second stage of labor -> pressure on the fetal head -> cephalohematoma formation -> 90% confidence. CHAIN: Vacuum-assisted vaginal delivery -> increased risk of cephalohematoma due to the application of suction -> 85% confidence. CHAIN: Soft, nonpulsatile swelling over the left parietal bone that does not cross suture lines -> characteristic of cephalohematoma -> 95% confidence. CHAIN: Apgar scores of 9 and 10 at 1 and 5 minutes -> reassuring scores, not indicative of a severe underlying condition -> 90%
enhanced_information: The most likely diagnosis for the soft, nonpulsatile swelling over the left parietal bone in the newborn is cephalohematoma. This is supported by the prolonged second stage of labor and vacuum-assisted vaginal delivery, which increase the risk of cephalohematoma formation. The characteristic location and appearance of the swelling align with cephalohematoma. The retrieved evidence path linking the location to cephalohematoma due to birth trauma further supports this diagnosis.
analysis: The most likely diagnosis for the soft, nonpulsatile swelling over the left parietal bone in the newborn, considering the prolonged second stage of labor and vacuum-assisted vaginal delivery, is cephalohematoma. Cephalohematoma is a subperiosteal hemorrhage that does not cross suture lines and is commonly associated with birth trauma. The location and characteristics of the swelling align with cephalohematoma in this case.
